readerQuestion: Should Home Assistant stay on my main network or join the IoT VLAN, and how do I keep discovery, control, and isolation working?
directAnswer: Start with one interface. For a small new setup, keep same-network-dependent devices together. In an existing segmented home, assess each integration's routed control and update requirements before moving the server. A second interface is an advanced exposure decision, not an automatic firewall boundary. Matter needs local IPv6 and the documented border-router path.
originalContribution: A three-layout decision table distinguishes same-segment exposure from routed rules and multi-interface access. A fictional first-generation Shelly lamp example separates commands, device-initiated CoIoT updates, phone UI access, and unrelated IoT traffic. The six-step procedure begins with a reversible plan and ends with non-critical command, physical-state and reconnect checks. It does not present a universal router ruleset.

claimChecks.claim: Discovery interface selection uses the Network integration and route-based auto-detection. This setting is not itself a firewall policy.
Zeroconf browser and selected discovery interfaces reveal mDNS services; absence alone does not identify the cause of a device problem.
The SSDP browser is available under Settings, System, Network and reports a different discovery mechanism.
Network HomeKit accessories across VLANs require mDNS reflection for discovery/pairing; paired-state and other prerequisites also matter.
Cast does not recommend/support automatic discovery across subnets. It describes forwarding or known hosts as alternatives, requires Container host mode, and has a separate media playback path.
The documented Linux Container installation uses host networking. That does not attach the host to an additional VLAN.

Matter needs local IPv6 and multicast. Troubleshooting recommends a shared LAN for Home Assistant, Wi-Fi Matter devices, and the relevant Thread border-router LAN connection. A Thread radio mesh is not the same thing as the LAN VLAN.

Generation 1 Shelly uses CoIoT, recommends unicast with the HA address and UDP 5683 default, and needs a restart after peer changes. Later generations use RPC and have different requirements; custom CoAP ports are possible.

pfSense interface rules filter in the inbound direction, are stateful by default, and allow matching replies through state. New device-initiated traffic must be evaluated separately. The article does not assume all routers have the same interface UI or rule ordering.
